title: Employment Situation (Feb 2027 data) — 08:30 ET, the statistically ordinary payroll that immediately follows the year's most amplified one
source: EST: derived from BLS's own scheduling rule — release on the third Friday following the end of the reference week, the Sun-Sat week containing the 12th. THE RULE WAS RE-IMPLEMENTED FROM SCRATCH BY THIS EVENT'S OWN never-assessed RESEARCH (2026-09-10) and validated against TWO BLS PRIMARIES RETRIEVED THIS SESSION, neither of them a sibling ledger. (1) bls.gov/schedule/news_release/empsit.htm, HTTP 200 via WebFetch 2026-09-10, 13 reference months Nov 2025 - Nov 2026: the rule plus its one documented holiday correction reproduces 10 of 13, and 10 OF 10 FROM THE FEBRUARY 2026 REFERENCE MONTH ONWARD. The three misses are the 2025 shutdown displacement chain (Nov 2025 data released 2025-12-16, Dec 2025 data 2026-01-09, Jan 2026 data 2026-02-11) and that chain CONVERGED BACK TO THE RULE at the February reference month — this event's own reference month, one year earlier. (2) bls.gov/bls/news-release/empsit.htm archive hrefs, HTTP 200 via WebFetch 2026-09-10, whose filenames encode the release date: of 16 February-data releases 1994-2010, the rule reproduces 12 EXACTLY, and all four misses are filenames encoding a Saturday or a Thursday — days the Employment Situation is not released on — so the pre-2000 history/ filename convention is not a release date, which is recorded as an unresolved limit rather than explained away. February 2027's 12th is a FRIDAY, so the reference week is Sun 2027-02-07 to Sat 2027-02-13 and the third Friday after 02-13 is 2027-03-05. NEITHER DOCUMENTED CORRECTION APPLIES: not a December reference month, and 2027-03-05 is not a federal holiday — an ordinary full NYSE session. Prefix is EST: and not BLS: because bls.gov has published no 2027 schedule at all: /schedule/news_release/2027_sched.htm returned HTTP 404 to WebFetch on 2026-09-10, and a derived date is not a published one
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN never-assessed RESEARCH (2026-09-10), superseding BOTH proposals/jobs-2027-03-05.from-jobs-2027-01-08.json and proposals/jobs-2027-03-05.from-jobs-2027-02-05.json, which stay where they are and are now shadowed. Both proposals were read first; their shared structural claim -- that this is the LAST payroll the March 2027 SEP meeting sees -- is confirmed against the FED: primary (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, HTTP 200 2026-09-10, page-stated 'Last Update: August 19, 2026': 2027 meets Jan 26-27, Mar 16-17*, Apr 27-28, Jun 8-9*, Jul 27-28, Sep 14-15*, Oct 26-27, Dec 7-8*, asterisk = Summary of Economic Projections). THE HEADLINE IS A REFUSAL, AND IT IS THE POINT. Measured on Yahoo split/dividend-adjusted daily bars 1993-2026 over SPY/QQQ/TLT/IEF/SHY/LQD/AGG/HYG/^VIX (380 usable payroll sessions, 34 March-released): THE MARCH-RELEASED PAYROLL IS STATISTICALLY ORDINARY ON EVERY INSTRUMENT. Zero of 18 primary tests (nine symbols x two controls) reach p<0.05 -- SPY 1.39x other payrolls (p=0.179) and 1.40x the ten nearest other March sessions (p=0.105); the lowest p anywhere is AGG at 0.080. SPY leave-one-out is significant in 0 OF 34 year-drops, and the only nominal era hit (<=2002, 2.50x, p=0.032) collapses to 1.15x in 2003-2009 and 1.26x in 2010-2026. D+1 1.13x (p=0.64), forward 10-session RV 1.14x (p=0.26), direction 21/34 (p=0.23), and March clears the all-payroll 95th percentile 2 of 34 against 1.7 expected. THE CALIBRATION FINDING THE WHOLE jobs-* SERIES NEEDED: a month's amplification RANK is close to uninformative at n~34. Bootstrapping the payroll days 2,000x, SPY's March rank 4/12 carries a 90% CI of [1..10] and SPY's February rank 1/12 carries [1..8]; TLT's February rank spans [1..11]. Rank is decoration, the significance test is the evidence -- which is why February's call survives (it rested on p=0.0015 against its tight local control and 34/34 leave-one-out, both independently REPRODUCED here at 1.93x SPY and 1.69x HYG against the sibling's 1.94x/1.70x) and March's cannot be made. TWO NEW HYPOTHESES TESTED AND REFUTED, so no later lane re-proposes them: (a) a quad-witching runway -- payrolls whose next opex is quarterly vs monthly -- SPY 1.11x (p=0.737), QQQ 0.93x, HYG 0.83x, IEF 1.19x, TLT 1.04x, every p>=0.34; (b) the projection-round framing -- payrolls before an SEP meeting vs a non-SEP one, 2008-2026, n=75/134 -- SPY 0.96x (p=0.943), all five instruments p>=0.25, which extends jobs-2027-09-03's days-to-FOMC kill to a different variable. THE RUNWAY RESULT IS THE DIRECT INVERSE OF FEBRUARY'S: this print's runway to opex-2027-03-19 is the LONG mode, 10 sessions (21 of 34 historical March payrolls; the other 13 run 5 sessions, a mechanical consequence of the rule emitting a date as late as the 12th), and over a length-matched 11-bar window the long-runway March print takes 3.1% of SPY realized variance against a 4.2% March null (0.74x, p=0.657) -- where February took 12.9% against 5.4% (2.40x, p=0.034). One nominal hit in the whole document, IEF long-runway share 2.15x (p=0.046), is left unacted-on as multiple-comparison noise and carries its own falsifier. The one MIXED leg: QQQ's move relative to SPY's COMPRESSES on March payrolls -- paired median QQQ/SPY 1.055 vs 1.383 on every other payroll, 0.76x, p=0.094 -- a hint, not a finding, registered as a forward test labelled not-significant. Corridor: D-4 from nerc-computational-load-phase-ii-workplan-2027-03-01 and uk-fuel-duty-rise-2027-03-01, SAME DAY as sp-rebalance-proforma-2027-03-05, D+1 to fomc-blackout-start-2027-03-06 (the blackout framing is cited as already refuted by jobs-2027-09-03 and deliberately NOT re-run), D+4 to eia-steo-2027-03-09, D+11 to fomc-2027-03-17 and D+14 to the quarterly opex-2027-03-19. Both house playbook docs grep to ZERO hits for payroll/nonfarm/NFP/employment-situation/first-friday and zero for quad-witch/projection-round. Impact high matches every other jobs-* entry; symbols [] matches them too. Estimates widen caution and license no entry.
